newsitem.title: GERMANY: Court lifts Premiere pay-TV injunction vs Kirch.
newsitem.headline: Court lifts Premiere pay-TV injunction vs Kirch.

text.p: A Munich court has lifted an injunction won by pay-TV broadcaster Premiere which had barred Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch from broadcasting major films on his DF1 digital channel, DF1 said on Thursday.
The ruling marks another twist in a battle by Kirch and publishing group Bertelsmann to win control of the fledgling German digital pay TV market.
Bertelsmann owns 37.5 percent and Kirch a quarter of Premiere, but the two have fallen out with each other and are now pursuing separate digital television projects.
In a second ruling, DF1 said it won an injunction stopping Premiere from carrying advertising for a new digital channel because it could not, as stated, be received nationwide.

Premiere said it originally sought the injunction because Kirch was not fulfilling his obligation of loyalty as a shareholder as it was promoting a competitor. But it was lifted because it was not filed on time, Premiere said.
Premiere added in a statement that it still planned to pursue the case against Kirch.

Kirch's DF1 promised a winter of first-run blockbusting movies on its CINEDOM pay-per-view service, which offers viewers the chance to watch the films at different starting times throughout the day at a cost of around six marks.

Despite the apparent setback for Premiere, the number of subscribers to Kirch's DF1 has proved disappointing since the channel's launch in July, while Premiere subscriber numbers have risen thanks to its live Bundesliga soccer broadcasts.
